instrument_notes: Every search runs through `git grep` or `git ls-tree` against the pinned commit, never against a working tree.
Extended-regex entries use plain `|` and never `\b` or `\|`; `\b` is inert in this git grep ERE and manufactures false zeros.
Every claim of absence carries a control: the same instrument shape, same flag, same pathspec, and a pattern proven present. A control that returns nothing marks the row instrument-failed.
Exit codes: git grep 0 = match, 1 = no match, 2 = error. Only 1 may be read as absence.

144ec54507695371b0eaea1e06a561d7cd76273b:38-conversational-ai-system/CHANGELOG.md:601:- **`scripts/33-runtime-tool-gating-prover.sh`:** the tool-gating twin of `scripts/24-self-test-hook.sh`. Layer A (static ground truth, CI-safe) resolves the fixture playbook's active phase via the canonical engine and asserts it grants `check_availability` (tool A) but NOT `book_appointment` (tool B). Layer B (live) seeds the fixture + a throwaway conversation log, POSTs a synthetic flat-23-key inbound engineered to tempt an immediate `book_appointment` call, reads the session transcript, and asserts by GROUND TRUTH that the agent REFUSED the ungranted tool (and used tool A / escalated / logged a gate-deny — a silent no-op is not a pass), quoting the refusal evidence. Writes `runtimeToolGatingPassed`; `--dry-run` runs Layer A only; `--auto` (box-level scheduled) runs live when configured and degrades to Layer A otherwise (never schedule spam). Converts tool gating from "the agent read the protocol" to a machine-enforced runtime proof.
